notes: Our own reading of the IEA's Energy and AI and LBNL's 2025 US data centre report, reviewed 2026-09-26. A total, an AI portion and a share only where the publisher states them; a computed share divides two stated figures.

records.statement: Neither the IEA nor LBNL counts datacentres, AI or otherwise.

records.ai_definition: Accelerated servers, those with GPUs or other AI accelerator chips.
records.statement: 30.9 million servers installed in US datacentres in 2024, including 4.2 million accelerated servers.
records.document: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update (June 2026), p.17

records.ai_definition: Electricity used by accelerated servers, which the IEA uses as a proxy for AI and describes as imperfect.
records.statement: Around 415 TWh in 2024, about 1.5% of global electricity demand. Accelerated servers accounted for 15% of it.
192 TWh in 2024, 4.7% of US electricity, excluding cryptocurrency mining. An AI share is stated only for 2030: 55% in the reference case.
records.document: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update (June 2026), pp.8 and 25

records.statement: Around 560 billion litres a year: about two thirds through electricity generation and fuel supply, a quarter in cooling on site, the rest in chip manufacture. No AI portion is given.
